subject: Interaction effects in models with latent variables

messages.author: 035e39d68f43a06c
messages.subject: Interaction effects in models with latent variables
parts:
Hey,

i am currently writing my bachelor thesis and have to analyze empirical data with R.
this is the code i am using


# Befehle SEM

# Interaktionseffekte in Modelle mit latenten Variablen

# lagged effects, CM, WFC zu T1| A,FT,L zu T2

# Befehl startet lavaan, jedes Mal anwenden

library(lavaan)


# Daten einlesen

# Daten werden eingelesen und in Tabellenform dargestellt

#header=T teilt R mit, dass die erste Zeile die Namen der Variablen enthält

read.csv2("/Users/moritzdorau/Desktop/Uni PB/Bachelorarbeit/Datensatz/Datensatz_neu.csv", header=T, sep=";")


# den eigenebenen Daten geben Sie einen Namen, damit sie als R-Objekt verfügbar sind

wfcdata <- read.csv2("/Users/moritzdorau/Desktop/Uni PB/Bachelorarbeit/Datensatz/Datensatz_neu.csv")

# Recodierung negativ formulierter Variablen

library(car)

wfcdata$cm02r <- recode(wfcdata$cm02,"0='4'; 1='3';2='2' ; 3='1'; 4='0'")

wfcdata$t2cm02r <- recode(wfcdata$t2cm02, "0='4'; 1='3';2='2'; 3='1'; 4='0'")



# Auffinden von Fehlern

str(wfcdata)

names(wfcdata) # listet alle Variablennamen auf


# Ausgabe deskriktiver Statistik, zuvor muss das Paket "psych" aufgerufen werden

library(psych)

describe(wfcdata) 


#__________________________________________________________________________________________________


# 1.) einzelne Produktterme werden für jede Kombination der jeweils drei Indikatoren/ Items (wfc1, wfc03, - cm01r,, cm03) gebildet

wfcdata$pt11 <- wfcdata$wfc01 * wfcdata$cm01r

wfcdata$pt13 <- wfcdata$wfc01 * wfcdata$cm03

wfcdata$pt31 <- wfcdata$wfc03 * wfcdata$cm01r

wfcdata$pt33 <- wfcdata$wfc03 * wfcdata$cm03


# 2.) Regression jedes Produktterms auf alle first-order-Effekt-Indikatoren und Speicherung im Datensatz

wfcdata$res11 <- resid (lm(pt11 ~ wfc01+wfc03 + cm01r+cm03, data=wfcdata,na.action = na.exclude))

wfcdata$res13 <- resid (lm(pt13 ~ wfc01+wfc03 + cm01r+cm03, data=wfcdata,na.action = na.exclude))

wfcdata$res31 <- resid (lm(pt31 ~ wfc01+wfc03 + cm01r+cm03, data=wfcdata,na.action = na.exclude))

wfcdata$res33 <- resid (lm(pt33 ~ wfc01+wfc03 + cm01r+cm03, data=wfcdata,na.action = na.exclude))


# Tests, die sicherstellen, dass keine Fehler auftreten

#Mittelwerte der Indikatoren sollen exakt null sein

mean(wfcdata$res11,na.rm=TRUE)

mean(wfcdata$res13,na.rm=TRUE)

mean(wfcdata$res31,na.rm=TRUE)

mean(wfcdata$res33,na.rm=TRUE)


# Ausgabe deskriktiver Statistik, zuvor muss das Paket "psych" aufgerufen werden

library(psych)

describe(wfcdata) 


# die Korrelationen sollten mit den first-order-Effekt-Indikatoren Null und unter den Produktterm-Indikatoren substantiell sein

modvar <- wfcdata[c("wfc01","wfc03","cm01r","cm03","res11","res13","res31", "res33")]

round(cor(modvar,use="pair"),2)


# 3.) Spezifikation des Modells für die abhängige Variable Fluktuation

intlat <-'

CM=~ cm01r+cm03

WFC=~ wfc01+wfc03

FT2=~ t2cm02r+t2ft04

A2=~ t2a02+t2a03+t2a04+t2a05

L2=~ t2l01+t2l02+t2l03r+t2l04+t2l05r+t2l06+t2l07r+t2l08

L=~ l01+l02+l03r+l04+l05r+l06+l07r+l08

A=~ a02+a03+a04+a05

FT=~ cm02r+ft04


Produktterm =~ res11+res13+res31+res33

Produktterm~~0*WFC

Produktterm~~0*CM


cm02r~~ t2cm02r

ft04~~ t2ft04

L2~~A2

A2~~FT2

FT2~~L2


# Messfehler-Kovarianzen derjenigen Produktterm-Indikatoren, die gemeinsame Elemente enthalten

# a) Erste Komponenten ist identisch (in res11, res13)

res11~~res13

# res31, res33

res31~~res33

# b) Zweite Komponente ist identisch (in res11, res 31)

res11~~res31

# res13

res13~~res33


#Strukturmodell

L2~ WFC + CM + Produktterm + L

A2~ WFC + CM + Produktterm + A

FT2~WFC + CM + Produktterm + FT

'

fit <- sem(intlat, data=wfcdata, missing="fiml",estimator="mlr")

summary(fit)



Unfortunately, i get always get the following error which i don't understand:

Fehler in chol.default(S) : 
  der führende Minor der Ordnung 33 ist nicht positiv definit
Zusätzlich: Warnmeldungen:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some cases are empty and will be removed:
  5 6 9 12 13 14 20 22 29 30 36 66 68 71 72 84 92 94 100 105 107 108 109 110 111 119 136 166 240 269 274 286 374
2: In computeOmega(Sigma.hat = Sigma.hat, Mu.hat = Mu.hat, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lav_model_gradient: Sigma.hat is not positive definite

3: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

4: In computeOmega(Sigma.hat = Sigma.hat, Mu.hat = Mu.hat, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lav_model_gradient: Sigma.hat is not positive definite

Maybe can give me some advise what to change!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Interaction effects in models with latent variables
parts:
> Unfortunately, i get always get the following error which i don't
> understand:

> Fehler in chol.default(S) :
> der führende Minor der Ordnung 33 ist nicht positiv definit

'S' is the observed sample covariance matrix. It would seem that it is
not positive definite. Perhaps this is due to the product-terms that are
included.

Have a look at the semTools package. In particular the indProd()
function, to construct product-terms.

> Zusätzlich: Warnmeldungen:
> 1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label =
> group.label, :
> lavaan WARNING: some cases are empty and will be removed:
> 5 6 9 12 13 14 20 22 29 30 36 66 68 71 72 84 92 94 100 105 107 108
> 109 110 111 119 136 166 240 269 274 286 374

This is a warning saying that all these cases are simply empty: only
missing values (at least for the observed variables used in the model).

> 2: In computeOmega(Sigma.hat = Sigma.hat, Mu.hat = Mu.hat,
> lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, :
> lav_model_gradient: Sigma.hat is not positive definite

This (and all following warnings) are a result of S not being positive
definite to begin with.

So, before you even begin with lavaan, you need to ensure that the
sample-based covariance of the all the observed variables that will be
included in the model, is positive definite.

Yves.
